title: Rookwatch passdown — triage and temporary fixes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal passdown notes for the Rookwatch overnight shift. Mostly scratchpad for triage steps and short-lived fixes — not canonical runbook. Save any permanent fixes as PRs and Confluence updates.

Top-of-shift summary (what I saw at 03:00 UTC):
- CPU spike on provisioner-2 around 01:10 — resolved by autoscaler, no user-facing errors observed.
- Alert: embedding-ingest queue grew to ~800 items between 00:30–01:00, backpressure engaged; workers auto-stretched but latency spiked to ~4s/token for a 2048 prompt.
- One Dedicated customer reported intermittent 503s (ticket JD-822) - looks correlated with region-us-west-2 transient networking.
- Small regressions in model-mem usage after last restart window — low priority, tracking in RDW-4532.

Things to check first if waking up to alerts:
1) Pager summary: which service? check PagerDuty incident message and first event.
2) Kibana quick search: service:{{service-name}} and error:5xx or error:timeout. Time range +10m from first alert.
3) Grafana dashboard: "Rookwatch — request-latency" and "Batcher — queue-length" for the last hour. Note if latency rises before queue growth or vice versa.
4) Check autoscaler events (infra-autoscaler logs) for OOM/kills or node provisioning failures.
5) If Dedicated customer is involved, verify whether traffic routed to dedicated pool — check routing logs (console -> routing -> recent decisions).

Quick triage checklist (shorthand commands I use):
- kubectl -n infra logs deploy/batcher --since=15m | tail -n 200  # look for throttling/backpressure
- curl -sS http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query="increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])" | jq .  # quick prom check (adjust query)
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:role,Values=gpu-worker" --region us-west-2  # if node capacity suspected
- gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 50  # GCP clusters

Temporary mitigation recipes (fast, non-invasive):
- Slow-path: Reduce batcher max-batch-size to lower memory pressure: edit configmap batcher-config -> set max_size: 64 then rollout restart batcher deployment. Observe latency tradeoff.
- Cache flush: If KV cache suspected corrupted (rare) — rotate cache key prefix for a small percentage of traffic (canary) rather than flush globally. TODO: document prefix rotation command.
- Fallback routing: For host-level faults, flip route policy to fallback-model:lightweight for 10% traffic to relieve heavy models. Use console rollout -> new policy -> staged 10%.

Escalation contacts (if on-call escalation needed):
- On-call infra lead: Riley Gomez (pager) — network and autoscaler problems.
- Serving runtime: Priya Menon (slack DM) — kernel/attention regressions and model memory issues.
- CTO on call for major customer-impacting incidents: Asha Patel (email + pager).

Known gotchas / recent fixes to watch for:
- Kernel upgrade 2026-03-09 introduced slight behavior change in kvcache eviction ordering. If you see cache-miss storms after restarts, roll back to kernel 1.8.2 or apply the hotfix (PR #672).
- Autoscaler sometimes reports "failed to attach volume" in us-west-2 when provisioning ephemeral GPU nodes — AWS API rate limits. If provisioning fails repeatedly, trigger temporary capacity shift to east region via routing policy.

Short-lived commands & snippets to copy-paste (keeps me fast):
- Restart batcher gracefully: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/batcher --timeout=10m
- Shrink pool (emergency): terraform apply -var='scale_down=true' -target=module.dedicated_pool["us-west-2"]
  # use with caution — coordinate with CS if Dedicated customers present
- Re-route 10% traffic to fallback: curl -X POST "https://console/redwood/api/policy/rollout" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"policy":"fallback-model:lightweight","percent":10}'

Notes-to-self: tests and follow-ups to create tomorrow:
- Write a short Confluence note on KV prefix rotation and a safe command for canary toggles. Linked artifact placeholder: confluence:ops/rookwatch-passdown
- Open PR to make batcher max_size adjustable by route instead of global config (RDW-4610).
- Investigate why ingest queue spikes between 00:20–01:00 consistently (could be a cron job alignment from customer ingestion windows).

If you take over mid-incident: what I would do in first 15 minutes:
- Confirm incident scope and blast radius (which customers, which regions).
- Capture timestamps and take screenshots of the key graphs. Paste them into PD incident ticket.
- Apply a small, reversible mitigation (reduce batch size OR flip 10% fallback) and observe for 5–7 minutes.
- If improvement, increase mitigations incrementally and notify CS/gen-seat for impacted customers.

Things that are explicitly out-of-scope for these notes:
- Permanent config changes (don’t edit permanent routing policies without filing a change request).
- Deep kernel debugging — unless Priya is available.

Closing reminders for next shift:
- If you had to revert the kernel, leave a TODO in RDW-4532 and tag Priya.
- Save any useful query snippets to Confluence snippet library (label: "rookwatch-snippets").
- If you flipped routing for a customer, follow up with CS to create a postmortem and ensure the customer knows the temporary measures.

Random scratch (notes-to-self that may become formal):
- Could we expose a simple "emergency throttle" toggle in Console to reduce batcher concurrency per-customer? Would reduce blast radius on ingest storms. Sketch in product-ops ticket.

End-of-shift quick checklist to pass down:
- State of alerts (none / degraded / major)
- Any mitigations applied (list commands and time applied)
- Tickets opened and owners
- Things to monitor closely for the next 4 hours

-- Marcus L. (leave me a Slack DM if unclear)
